**Wilbur Louis Ross Jr.** (born November 28, 1937) is an American businessman who served as the 39th [United States secretary of commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Commerce "United States Secretary of Commerce") from 2017 to 2021. A member of the [Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"), Ross was previously chairman and chief executive officer of [WL Ross & Co](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WL_Ross_&_Co "WL Ross & Co") from 2000 to 2017.

Ross ran the bankruptcy restructuring practice at [N M Rothschild & Sons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N_M_Rothschild_&_Sons "N M Rothschild & Sons") in New York beginning in the late 1970s. In the 1990s, Ross was an adviser to New York City mayor [Rudy Giuliani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudy_Giuliani "Rudy Giuliani") on privatization, and was appointed by U.S. president [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") to the board of [the U.S. Russia Investment Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_U.S._Russia_Investment_Fund "The U.S. Russia Investment Fund"). In 2000, he left Rothschild to found WL Ross & Co. Ross was a banker known for acquiring and restructuring failed companies in industries such as steel, coal, telecommunications and textiles, later selling them for a profit after operations improved, a record that had earned him the moniker "King of Bankruptcy".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-king-1) Ross has been chairman or lead director of more than 100 companies operating in more than 20 countries. In 2017, Ross became commerce secretary in the [Donald Trump administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "First presidency of Donald Trump"); at age 79, Ross was the oldest first-time Cabinet appointee in U.S. history.

## Early life and education

Ross was born on November 28, 1937, in [Weehawken, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weehawken,_New_Jersey "Weehawken, New Jersey"), and grew up in nearby [North Bergen, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Bergen,_New_Jersey "North Bergen, New Jersey").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-bottomfeederking-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-3) His father, Wilbur Louis Ross, was a lawyer who later became a judge, and his mother, Agnes (née O'Neill), of [Irish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_people "Irish people") descent, was [valedictorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valedictorian "Valedictorian") at Sacred Heart Academy in Hoboken and taught [third grade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_grade "Third grade") in North Bergen for 40 years.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-bottomfeederking-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-4)

Ross attended [Xavier High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_High_School_(New_York_City) "Xavier High School (New York City)"), a [Catholic school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_school "Catholic school"), and [college-preparatory school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College-preparatory_school "College-preparatory school") in Manhattan. He ran track and was captain of the rifle team. He graduated in 1955.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-Xavier-5) In 1959, he received a bachelor's degree from [Yale College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_College "Yale College"), his father's alma mater.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-fastfacts-6) At Yale, Ross edited one of the literary magazines and worked at the radio station. His dream was to be a writer. He enrolled in an English course that required writing a thousand words by 10 a.m. every day; after two weeks, he ran out of things to write about and dropped the course.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-8) His faculty adviser at Yale helped him get his first summer job on [Wall Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_Street "Wall Street"). In 1961, he received a [Master of Business Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Business_Administration "Master of Business Administration") degree at [Harvard Business School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Business_School "Harvard Business School").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-IsWilburCrazy-9)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-fastfacts-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-10)

## Business career

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Carlos_Menem_with_Wilbur_Ross.jpg/250px-Carlos_Menem_with_Wilbur_Ross.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Carlos_Menem_with_Wilbur_Ross.jpg)Ross with [Carlos Menem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Menem "Carlos Menem") in 1997

### Early career

In 1963, he joined what became Wood, Struthers & [Winthrop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Winthrop_(banker) "Robert Winthrop (banker)"). There, he liquidated the portfolio of its [venture capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venture_capital "Venture capital") affiliate.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-euro-11)

He then worked for [Faulkner, Dawkins & Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faulkner,_Dawkins_&_Sullivan "Faulkner, Dawkins & Sullivan"), an institutional [securities research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Securities_research "Securities research") company, where he rose to become president of its [investment banking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investment_banking "Investment banking") operation. The firm was sold to what became [Shearson Lehman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shearson_Lehman "Shearson Lehman").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-euro-11)

### Rothschild Investments

In 1976, Ross began his 24-year employment with the [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") office of [Rothschild & Co](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rothschild_&_Co "Rothschild & Co"), where he ran the [bankruptcy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bankruptcy "Bankruptcy") [restructuring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restructuring "Restructuring") advisory practice.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-bottomfeederking-2)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-trumppal-12) By 1998, Ross was involved in eight of the 25 biggest bankruptcies to date, including [Drexel Burnham Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drexel_Burnham_Lambert "Drexel Burnham Lambert"), [Texaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texaco "Texaco"), Public Service of New Hampshire (now [Eversource Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eversource_Energy "Eversource Energy")), and [Eastern Air Lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Air_Lines "Eastern Air Lines").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-euro-11)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-13)

In the 1980s, [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump")'s three casinos in [Atlantic City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_City "Atlantic City") were under threat of [foreclosure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreclosure "Foreclosure") from lenders. Ross, who was then the senior managing director of Rothschild & Co, represented investors in the casino. Along with [Carl Icahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Icahn "Carl Icahn"), Ross convinced bondholders to strike a deal that allowed Trump to keep control of the casinos.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-trumppal-12)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-14)

### WL Ross & Co.

Main article: [WL Ross & Co](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WL_Ross_&_Co "WL Ross & Co")

In November 1997, under Rothschild & Co, Ross started a $200 million fund to invest in [distressed securities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distressed_securities "Distressed securities"). In its first year, it earned a 15.2% return.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-euro-11) In April 2000, just before the [dot-com bubble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot-com_bubble "Dot-com bubble") burst, Ross founded WL Ross & Co and raised $450 million to buy the fund from Rothschild and make additional investments.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-trumppal-12)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-bottomfeederking-2) By 2003, the fund had averaged a 30% return.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-15)

In 2006, Ross sold WL Ross & Co to Amvescap (now [Invesco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invesco "Invesco")).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-17)

#### International Steel Group (ISG)

In February 2002, WL Ross & Co founded [International Steel Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Steel_Group "International Steel Group"). He first agreed to buy the assets of bankrupt [Ling-Temco-Vought](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ling-Temco-Vought "Ling-Temco-Vought") for $325 million, paying $11 per ton of capacity when other firms were trading for $200 per ton of capacity.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-18) A few weeks later, [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush") slapped a 30% tariff on many types of imported steel. A year later, WL Ross & Co acquired the assets of bankrupt [Bethlehem Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethlehem_Steel "Bethlehem Steel"). As part of the bankruptcy reorganizations, these companies shifted their huge pension liabilities to the government-backed [Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pension_Benefit_Guaranty_Corporation "Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-bottomfeederking-2)

Ross had support from the [United Steelworkers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Steelworkers "United Steelworkers"), negotiating a deal to save some jobs.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-IsWilburCrazy-9)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-19)

In April 2005, WL Ross & Co sold [International Steel Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Steel_Group "International Steel Group") to [Mittal Steel Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mittal_Steel_Company "Mittal Steel Company") for $4.5 billion, half in cash and half in stock, and made 12.5 times its original investment.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-20) Ross personally made a $260 million profit on his $3 million investment and gained a seat on the board of directors of Mittal Steel.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-21)

#### International Textile Group (ITG)

After outbidding [Warren Buffett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Buffett "Warren Buffett"), who offered $579 million, WL Ross & Co acquired [Burlington Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burlington_Industries "Burlington Industries") for $620 million and combined it with [Cone Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cone_Mills "Cone Mills") in 2004 to form [International Textile Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Textile_Group "International Textile Group").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-22)

In 2005, Ross acquired 77.3% of Safety Components International for $51.2 million.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-23)

In October 2006, Ross had [International Textile Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Textile_Group "International Textile Group") acquire Safety Components International. Ross controlled both companies and in February 2014, Ross paid $81 million to settle a lawsuit brought by shareholders that Ross breached his [fiduciary duty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiduciary_duty "Fiduciary duty") when structuring the merger.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-24) [International Textile Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Textile_Group "International Textile Group") was acquired by [private equity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_equity "Private equity") firm [Platinum Equity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_Equity "Platinum Equity") in 2016.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-25)

#### International Automotive Components Group (IAC)

International Automotive Components Group was formed in 2006 by WL Ross & Co and investment funds managed by [Franklin Templeton Investments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_Templeton_Investments "Franklin Templeton Investments").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-26) In 2006, the company acquired the European operations of [Lear Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lear_Corporation "Lear Corporation")[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-27) and in 2007, it acquired Lear's North American interiors operations.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-28) In 2005–2007, IAC purchased several divisions of [Collins & Aikman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collins_&_Aikman "Collins & Aikman").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-29) In September 2005, investors led by Ross invested $100 million in Oxford Automotive for 25% of the company.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-30) In 2006, Oxford merged with [Wagon Automotive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wagon_Automotive "Wagon Automotive").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-31)

#### International Coal Group (ICG)

WL Ross & Co founded [International Coal Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Coal_Group "International Coal Group") in 2004 after acquiring the assets of several bankrupt coal companies. The [United Mine Workers of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Mine_Workers_of_America "United Mine Workers of America") protested the reorganization as it led to changes in [health care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care "Health care") and [pensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pension "Pension") for the existing employees.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-32)

In 2006, the [Sago Mine disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sago_Mine_disaster "Sago Mine disaster"), an explosion in a coal mine indirectly owned by International Coal Group, likely caused by a [lightning strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightning_strike "Lightning strike"), led to the deaths of 12 miners.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-33) The mine had 12 roof collapses in 2005, and [U.S. Department of Labor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Labor "United States Department of Labor") data showed 208 [citations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citation "Citation") for safety violations in that same period, including 21 times for build-up of toxic gases.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-34) Miners and their families accused Ross of ignoring safety violations. Ross defended his company's management of the mine.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-35)

In 2011, [Arch Coal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arch_Coal "Arch Coal") acquired International Coal Group for $3.4 billion.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-36)

#### Navigator Gas

By January 2016, WL Ross & Co was the "biggest investor" in [Navigator Gas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navigator_Gas "Navigator Gas"), a liquefied gas shipping company.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-37)

### Overstating of net worth

In February 2017, *[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")* reported that Ross has a net worth of $2.5 billion. Financial disclosure forms filed by Ross after his nomination as Commerce Secretary showed less than $700 million in assets, and Forbes later revised his net worth to $600 million.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-phantom-38)

### Grift allegations

In August 2018, *[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")* reported that Ross's business partners and workers accused Ross of illicitly siphoning or stealing a total of $120 million.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-grifting-39)

In December 2017, a report by two Irish financial analysts, commissioned by [Luke Ming Flanagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Ming_Flanagan "Luke Ming Flanagan"), an Irish [member of the European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_the_European_Parliament "Member of the European Parliament"), accused Ross of [insider trading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insider_trading "Insider trading") as part of a 2014 sale of shares in the [Bank of Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ireland "Bank of Ireland") by WL Ross & Co.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-40)

### Overcharging of fees

In August 2016, Ross agreed to reimburse investors $11.8 million and pay a fine of $2.3 million to settle a [U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Securities_and_Exchange_Commission "U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission") probe into the overcharging of fees by WL Ross & Co. The company had self-reported the issue and did not admit any liability.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-41)

On August 7, 2018, five former WL Ross & Co. employees and investors claimed the firm was charging its investors fees on money it had lost, including allegedly charging fees on one investment that was essentially worthless.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-grifting-39)

## Secretary of Commerce (2017–2021)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/President_Donald_Trump_receives_a_briefing_on_a_military_strike.jpg/250px-President_Donald_Trump_receives_a_briefing_on_a_military_strike.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Donald_Trump_receives_a_briefing_on_a_military_strike.jpg)Secretary Ross during the April [2017 Shayrat missile strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Shayrat_missile_strike "2017 Shayrat missile strike") operation[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/President_Trump%27s_Trip_Abroad_%2834671273521%29.jpg/250px-President_Trump%27s_Trip_Abroad_%2834671273521%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Trump's_Trip_Abroad_(34671273521).jpg)Ross in [Riyadh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riyadh "Riyadh"), Saudi Arabia, May 2017

### Nomination and confirmation

On November 30, 2016, then-[President-elect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President-elect_of_the_United_States "President-elect of the United States") [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") announced that he would nominate Ross for [Secretary of Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Commerce "United States Secretary of Commerce").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-43) On February 27, 2017, the Senate confirmed Ross in a 72–27 vote.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-45) Ross was sworn into office on February 28, 2017.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-46)

Ross took office at the age of 79, making him the oldest first-time Cabinet appointee in U.S. history. The previous record-holder was another Secretary of Commerce, [Philip Klutznick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Klutznick "Philip Klutznick"), who took office in 1980 at the age of 72.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-47)

### Trade issues

#### UK trade post-Brexit

In December 2016, after being designated by Trump as his nominee to lead the Commerce Department, Ross said in a speech to Cypriot financiers that [Brexit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brexit "Brexit") was a "God-given opportunity" for other countries, such as Ireland and Germany, to draw business away from the [United Kingdom's financial services industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_services_in_the_United_Kingdom "Financial services in the United Kingdom").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-49) In 2017, Ross said that a trade deal with the UK was a low priority for the Trump administration; however, he outlined possible terms.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-51) No U.S. trade deal with the UK was concluded, although Ross and Treasury Secretary [Steve Mnuchin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Mnuchin "Steve Mnuchin") stated in January 2020 that they hoped to have an "easy" agreement with the UK that year.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-53)

#### Tariffs and trade wars

Further information: [First Trump tariffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Trump_tariffs "First Trump tariffs") and [China–United States trade war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China–United_States_trade_war "China–United States trade war")

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Secretary_Ross_Meets_with_Ministry_of_Commerce_Minister_Zhong_Shan_%2837050855080%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Ross_Meets_with_Ministry_of_Commerce_Minister_Zhong_Shan_%2837050855080%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Ross_Meets_with_Ministry_of_Commerce_Minister_Zhong_Shan_(37050855080).jpg)Ross with China's Commerce Minister [Zhong Shan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhong_Shan "Zhong Shan") (right)

In September 2017, Ross traveled to Beijing as part of efforts to de-escalate trade tensions between the United States and China.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-54) In February 2018, the Commerce Department recommended an increase of tariffs in aluminum and steel imports.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-56) On March 1, 2018, Trump implemented a 25% tariff on steel and a 10% tariff on aluminum imports.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-57) In September 2018, Ross said that the tariffs are meant to "modify China's behavior".[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-58)

In 2018, under Trump and Ross, the U.S. imposed tariffs on the import of steel and aluminum from the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union"), [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada"), and [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-Bryan-59) Ross dismissed concerns that the tariffs would increase costs to U.S. consumers, harm the U.S. economy, and damage relations with U.S. allies, saying that tariffs were "blips on the radar screen" and that the EU "will get over this in due course."[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-Bryan-59) He also dismissed concerns over EU retaliatory tariffs.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-Bryan-59) In November 2019, Ross indicated that the Trump administration might now also impose tariffs on imports of automobiles from the EU;[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-60) in January 2020, however, Ross said that the Trump administration might still impose tariffs on European cars despite ongoing trade talks.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-61) Also in January 2020, Ross threatened retaliation if the EU adopted a proposed [carbon tax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_tax "Carbon tax"), comparing it to a proposed EU [digital services tax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxation_of_digital_goods "Taxation of digital goods"), to which the administration has also threatened tariffs in response.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-62)

### Ban of Huawei

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/75/U.S._Commerce_Secretary_Wilbur_Ross%2C_Acting_Attorney_General_Matthew_Whitaker%2C_Homeland_Security_Secretary_Kirstjen_Nielsen%2C_FBI_Director_Christopher_Wray_Announces_23_Criminal_Charges_Against_China%27s_Huawei_%26_Wanzhou_Meng.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:U.S._Commerce_Secretary_Wilbur_Ross,_Acting_Attorney_General_Matthew_Whitaker,_Homeland_Security_Secretary_Kirstjen_Nielsen,_FBI_Director_Christopher_Wray_Announces_23_Criminal_Charges_Against_China's_Huawei_&_Wanzhou_Meng.jpg)[U.S. Department of Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Department_of_Commerce "U.S. Department of Commerce"), [U.S. Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Department_of_Justice "U.S. Department of Justice"), [Department of Homeland Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Homeland_Security "Department of Homeland Security") and [Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") announce 23 criminal charges against [PRC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PRC "PRC")'s [Huawei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huawei "Huawei") and [Wanzhou Meng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wanzhou_Meng "Wanzhou Meng").

In January 2019, Ross was present with other American politicians when 23 criminal charges were announced against [Huawei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huawei "Huawei") and its CFO [Meng Wanzhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meng_Wanzhou "Meng Wanzhou"), including [financial fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_crime#Fraud "Financial crime"), [money laundering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Money_laundering "Money laundering"), [conspiracy against the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspiracy_against_the_United_States "Conspiracy against the United States"), [industrial espionage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_espionage "Industrial espionage"), [mail and wire fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mail_and_wire_fraud "Mail and wire fraud"), [obstruction of justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obstruction_of_justice "Obstruction of justice") and violation of [sanctions against Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanctions_against_Iran "Sanctions against Iran"). In July 2019, Ross stated that the United States will keep Huawei on its blacklist but will allow licensed sales.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-64)

### Accusations of being out of touch

In May 2017, Ross accompanied Trump on his first foreign visit, to [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia"), where Ross generated controversy after heralding the president's visit as a success due to a lack of protests, unaware that the Saudis had banned public protest and demonstrations since 2011.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-66)

During the [2018–19 federal government shutdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018–19_United_States_federal_government_shutdown "2018–19 United States federal government shutdown"), Ross was criticized as being out of touch with average American citizens after expressing bewilderment about why furloughed, unpaid workers and contractors would choose to visit [food banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_bank "Food bank") rather than apply for a personal loan.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-68)

### Non-disclosures

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/Wilbur_Ross_-_2017.jpg/250px-Wilbur_Ross_-_2017.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wilbur_Ross_-_2017.jpg)The leaked documents revealed that Secretary of Commerce Wilbur Ross holds stakes in businesses connected to sanctioned [Russian oligarchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_oligarchs "Russian oligarchs"), which he did not disclose during his confirmation hearings.

In February 2019, Ross's financial disclosure was rejected by the [Office of Government Ethics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Office_of_Government_Ethics "United States Office of Government Ethics") after he reported that he had sold bank stock when in fact he held on to them.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-70)

Ross failed to disclose a lawsuit from ex-business partner David Storper on his financial disclosure forms. Ross settled the lawsuit for $9 million after being [subpoenaed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subpoena "Subpoena") for information that he did not want to disclose.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-71)

### Conflicts of interest from failure to divest

In June 2018, an investigation by *[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")* found that Ross, while Secretary of Commerce, owned "stakes in companies co-owned by the Chinese government, a shipping firm tied to [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin")'s inner circle, a Cypriot bank reportedly caught up in the [Robert Mueller investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mueller_special_counsel_investigation "Mueller special counsel investigation"), and that Ross had failed to divest his financial holdings, instead putting them in a trust for his family members, contradicting Ross's written statement in November 2017 that he had divested all his financial holdings.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-lies-72) Ross may have broken the law in doing so.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-lies-72) These holdings posed a conflict of interest for Ross, as the Trump administration was in a position to affect the value of the holdings.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-lies-72)

Ross was confirmed by the Senate in February 2017 and he agreed to sell his stocks before the end of May 2017. In July 2018, it was reported that Ross divested from his stock in [Invesco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invesco "Invesco"), originally worth between $10 million and $50 million, in December 2017. Between the end of May and the sale date in December, the value of Ross's holdings in Invesco increased by between approximately $1.2 million to $6 million, depending on the number of shares he owned, which was not disclosed. Ross said that he "mistakenly believed that all [his] previously held Invesco stock was sold".[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-73) On July 13, 2018, after he received a letter from the government's top ethics watchdog warning of "potential for a serious criminal violation", Ross announced that he will sell all his remaining stock.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-74)

In October 2018, documents showed that Ross had participated in a meeting with executives from [Chevron Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chevron_Corporation "Chevron Corporation") where they discussed oil and gas developments, tax reform and trade issues. Ross's wife owned a stake in Chevron worth at least $250,000 at the time.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-75)

In October 2020, it was reported that Ross had continued to serve on the board of a Chinese joint venture until January 2019 (which was nearly two years into his tenure as Secretary of Commerce); at the same time, the United States and China were engaged in a trade war.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-76)

### Insider trading allegations

While Secretary of Commerce, Ross [shorted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short_(finance) "Short (finance)") at least five stocks.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-shorted-77) In June 2018, it was revealed that Ross [shorted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short_(finance) "Short (finance)") stock after he knew of an upcoming report with information that would adversely affect the company but before the story was published. Ross later closed out the position at a substantial profit after the story was published.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-lies-72)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-negative-78) Ethics experts said that the shorting was alarming given that federal office-holders are prohibited from profiting on nonpublic information.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-negative-78) Ross denied that he had engaged in [insider trading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insider_trading "Insider trading").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-79) Ross had shorted two additional stocks in June 2018 and two additional stocks in July 2018.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-shorted-77)

### 2020 Census citizenship question

As Secretary of Commerce, Ross oversaw the [Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Bureau_of_the_Census "U.S. Bureau of the Census") and the [2020 Census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_Census "2020 United States Census"). In December 2017, he approved sending, in the form of a letter (which was originally drafted by [Thomas Hofeller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Hofeller "Thomas Hofeller"), a noted anti-immigrant political figure) that was later copied by James Uthmeier into a memo, a request to the Department of Justice to add a question to the Census for the first time since the 1940s asking about the U.S. citizenship status of the members of the responding household. Specifically, Ross sought to amend the decennial Census to add the controversial question: "Is this person a citizen of the United States?"[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-80)

New York solicitor general [Barbara Underwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Underwood "Barbara Underwood") led a lawsuit filed by 18 states and many cities to attempt to stop the Trump administration from adding a citizenship question on the 2020 Census.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-censusstay-82) The Department of Justice supported the Department of Commerce. [U.S. federal judge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_federal_judge "United States federal judge") [Jesse M. Furman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_M._Furman "Jesse M. Furman") ruled against the Department of Justice and Wilbur Ross, stating that if the trial is delayed the appeals process may not be done by summer 2019, the printing deadline of the census.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-censusstay-82) Furman blocked the census question proposal on January 15, 2019, saying Ross had violated a "veritable smorgasbord" of federal rules, asserting Ross and his aides made false or misleading statements under oath[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-83) and that he sought to add the question to the Census based on a pretext.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-NYTContempt-84) The House of Representatives held Ross in contempt of Congress and accused Ross of lying about the citizenship question's origins.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-PoliticoDesiderio-85) Specifically, Ross had testified under oath that the addition of the question was prompted by DOJ when in fact he had made the request via the Hofeller letter he had transmitted. It became known in July 2021 that the [Justice Department inspector general](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice_Office_of_the_Inspector_General "United States Department of Justice Office of the Inspector General") had determined Ross had misled Congress, but the Trump Justice Department declined to prosecute him.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-86)

#### Contempt of Congress

Ross and the Trump administration refused to comply with a [congressional subpoena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_subpoena "Congressional subpoena"), issued by the [House Oversight Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_Oversight_and_Reform "United States House Committee on Oversight and Reform"), for documents regarding efforts to add a citizenship question to the 2020 Census.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-87) After Trump asserted [executive privilege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_privilege "Executive privilege") over the subpoenaed documents, the House Oversight Committee voted to hold Ross and Attorney General [William Barr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Barr "William Barr") in criminal [contempt of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contempt_of_Congress "Contempt of Congress"), with the committee's chairman saying that Ross and Barr had "blatantly obstructed our ability to do [congressional oversight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_oversight "Congressional oversight")."[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-PoliticoDesiderio-85)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-NYTContempt-84) In June 2019, the House held Barr and Ross in contempt of Congress on a mostly party-line 230–198 vote; this was only the second time in U.S. history that a sitting Cabinet member was held in contempt.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-NYTContempt-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-PoliticoDesiderio-85) The vote signified an escalation of the House of Representatives' battles with the Trump White House over congressional oversight, but was largely symbolic as Trump's Justice Department did not act on the criminal citation.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-NYTContempt-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-PoliticoDesiderio-85)

#### Supreme Court decision

On June 27, 2019, the Supreme Court, in *[Department of Commerce v. New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Commerce_v._New_York "Department of Commerce v. New York")*, left the citizenship question blocked from the 2020 census, in part because of the government's explanation for why it was added.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-88) In the Supreme Court opinion,[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-89) there was a significant mismatch between Secretary Ross's decision to add the question, and his stated reason that the question would support Department of Justice's Voter Rights Act.

### Ownership in Navigator Gas

Main article: [Paradise Papers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradise_Papers "Paradise Papers")

In November 2017, leaked documents known as the [Paradise Papers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradise_Papers "Paradise Papers") showed that, during his confirmation hearings, Ross had failed to clearly disclose a financial interest in [Navigator Gas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navigator_Gas "Navigator Gas"), a shipping company which transports petrochemicals for Russian gas and petrochemicals company [Sibur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sibur "Sibur").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-icij-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-leaked-91) Ross had failed to clearly disclose ties to Russian interests during his confirmation hearings.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-leaked-91) While his confirmation was pending, Ross promised in a letter to the [Office of Congressional Ethics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Congressional_Ethics "Office of Congressional Ethics") to cut ties "with more than 80 financial entities in which he has interests". This letter played a key role in securing his confirmation. However, according to the leaked documents, while he did divest some holdings, he did not disclose the full extent of those he retained.

Speaking about his financial ties to Navigator, Ross said the media was making "a lot more out of it than it deserves" and "There is nothing wrong with it. The fact that it happens to be called a Russian company doesn't mean there is any evil in it."[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-92) A spokesman for Ross stated that Ross has never met Shamalov, Timchenko or Mikhelson and that Ross "recuses himself from any matters focused of transoceanic shipping vessels, but has been generally supportive of the administration's sanctions of Russian and Venezuelan entities".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-icij-90)

### Dysfunction of the Department of Commerce

In July 2019, *Politico* reported that the Commerce Department under Ross reached "new heights of distraction"; an outside source, as well as multiple senior staffers, described Ross as "seen as kind of irrelevant" and morale at the department as "very low because there's not a lot of confidence in the secretary." Ross allegedly left his department leaderless due to the large amounts of time spent in the White House trying to win support from President Trump. Also, Ross allegedly tended to fall asleep in meetings to the extent that senior staffers avoided putting him in critical meetings where he could fall asleep.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-93) Reports of Ross's inability to stay awake have gone back as far as May 2017, where in a meeting in [Riyadh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riyadh "Riyadh") with the Arab-Islam-American Summit during President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump")'s speech, Ross appeared to have been completely asleep.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-94)

### NOAA/Hurricane Dorian controversy

Further information: [Hurricane Dorian–Alabama controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian–Alabama_controversy "Hurricane Dorian–Alabama controversy") and [False or misleading statements by Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/False_or_misleading_statements_by_Donald_Trump "False or misleading statements by Donald Trump")

On September 1, 2019, President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that [Hurricane Dorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian "Hurricane Dorian") presented a major threat to [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama "Alabama"); minutes later the [Birmingham, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham,_Alabama "Birmingham, Alabama"), branch of the [National Weather Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Weather_Service "National Weather Service") (NWS) (which is under the [National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Oceanic_and_Atmospheric_Administration "National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration") (NOAA), which is part of the Commerce Department) reported that Alabama was not at risk.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-CommerceChief-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-FreemdmanSamenow-96) *The New York Times* reported that Ross had threatened, a few days late, to fire high-level NOAA staff unless the agency disavowed its contradiction of Trump's false claim,[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-CommerceChief-95)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-Duster-97) leading to a September 6 NOAA statement from an unidentified spokesperson endorsing Trump's position and declaring that the NWS Birmingham's contradiction of Trump was incorrect.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-CommerceChief-95) The Commerce Department denied that Ross had threatened to fire "any NOAA staff over forecasting and public statements about Hurricane Dorian."[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-Duster-97)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-98) Later reporting said that Ross had made the call from Greece, where he was traveling, after being told to "fix the problem" by acting White House chief of staff [Mick Mulvaney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Mulvaney "Mick Mulvaney"), reportedly on Trump's orders.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-99)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-WaPo-100) NOAA's disavowal prompted an outcry from scientists and others, who said that the agency's failure to back its hurricane forecasters damaged its credibility.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-FreemdmanSamenow-96)

A subsequent report by the [National Academy of Public Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Academy_of_Public_Administration_(United_States) "National Academy of Public Administration (United States)"), commissioned by NOAA, found that NOAA's leadership violated the agency's scientific integrity policy by releasing a statement backing Trump's false statement about [Hurricane Dorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian "Hurricane Dorian")'s path.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-101) The [Office of Inspector General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_inspector_general_(United_States) "Office of inspector general (United States)") (OIG) of the Commerce Department separately investigated the incident and concluded that the Commerce Department "ran a 'flawed process' that did not sufficiently engage NOAA and went against the interests of the agency and the National Weather Service."[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-FreemdmanSamenow-96) In a July 2020 letter to Ross, Inspector General Peggy Gustafson expressed "deep concern" that the department was blocking OIG from publicly releasing its report by asserting "amorphous and generalized privileges."[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-FreemdmanSamenow-96) The letter prompted Democratic Senator [Maria Cantwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Cantwell "Maria Cantwell"), the [ranking member](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranking_member "Ranking member") of the [Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Commerce,_Science,_and_Transportation "United States Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation"), to call upon Ross to "immediately cease this campaign to keep the public in the dark."[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-FreemdmanSamenow-96) The [House Science Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Committee_on_Science,_Space_and_Technology "House Committee on Science, Space and Technology") also probed Ross's role in the issuance of the NOAA statement.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-102)

### Coronavirus pandemic

In a January 30, 2020, interview with [Maria Bartiromo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Bartiromo "Maria Bartiromo") of [Fox Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Business "Fox Business"), when asked if the [COVID-19 outbreak in China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_mainland_China "COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China") would threaten the U.S. economy, Ross said, "I think it will help to accelerate the return of jobs to North America ... I don't want to talk about a victory lap over a very unfortunate, very malignant disease ... the fact is, it does give business yet another thing to consider when they go through their review of their supply chain."[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-103)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-104) The outbreak [became a pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States "COVID-19 pandemic in the United States"), and caused a [major recession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_recession "COVID-19 recession"), with 10 million Americans filing [unemployment claims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unemployment_insurance "Unemployment insurance") and unemployment rising more than during the entirety of the [Great Recession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Recession "Great Recession").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-105)

### 2020 Census count early completion

Due to delays and operation challenges brought about by the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States "COVID-19 pandemic in the United States"), Ross and [U.S. Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Census_Bureau "U.S. Census Bureau") director [Steven Dillingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Dillingham "Steven Dillingham") announced on April 13, 2020, that they would extend the timeframe for field data collection and self-response for the [2020 United States Census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_Census "2020 United States Census") to October 31, 2020.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-106) However, on August 3, 2020, the Census Bureau announced that they were moving this deadline up to September 30, 2020.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-GuardianCensus-107) Community advocates and former Census Bureau employees expressed concern that this shortened timeframe would result in poor-quality data and a significant undercount that would disproportionately affect traditionally hard-to-count groups such as ethnic minorities, young adults, and people living in rural areas.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-GuardianCensus-107)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-108)

On September 24, 2020, federal district court judge [Lucy Koh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucy_Koh "Lucy Koh") issued a preliminary injunction against the plan to end counting on September 30 rather than the scheduled October 31, saying the Commerce Department "never articulated a satisfactory explanation." She also blocked a plan to deliver the count results to the White House by December 31, rather than the original April 2021 delivery date when Trump might be out of office.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-109) On the next business day, Ross announced the count would end October 5, as the administration appealed Koh's decision to the [9th circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Court_of_Appeals_for_the_Ninth_Circuit "United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit"). Koh subsequently called the October 5 end date "a violation" of her court order and prepared to begin [contempt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contempt_of_court "Contempt of court") proceedings against Ross and the Commerce Department.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-110) The appeals court rejected the administration's appeal,[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-111) and the Census Bureau announced on October 2 that the count would continue until October 31.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-112) However, the counted ultimately ended at 11:59 PM on October 15 after the administration appealed to the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States"), which issued a 7–1 ruling allowing the count to finish early.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-113)

## Post-administration (2021–present)

On July 23, 2021, the Chinese government sanctioned Ross as part of "reciprocal counter-sanctions" after the U.S. government imposed sanctions on Hong Kong officials.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-114)

## Honors

In 1999, Ross was awarded the [Order of Industrial Service Merit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Industrial_Service_Merit "Order of Industrial Service Merit") medal by South Korean president [Kim Dae Jung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Dae_Jung "Kim Dae Jung") for his assistance during the [1997 Asian financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_Asian_financial_crisis "1997 Asian financial crisis").[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-115) He was awarded the [American Irish Historical Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Irish_Historical_Society "American Irish Historical Society") Gold Medal in 2014 in recognition of his work in Ireland and [Irish-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish-American "Irish-American") causes.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-116)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-Xavier-5) The [Japanese government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Japan "Government of Japan") awarded Ross the [Order of the Rising Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Rising_Sun "Order of the Rising Sun"), Gold and Silver Star, in recognition of his service as Chairman of the Board of New York's [Japan Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_Society_(Manhattan) "Japan Society (Manhattan)"), his work to promote and strengthen the Japanese economy, and his relief efforts after the [2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Tōhoku_earthquake_and_tsunami "2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-117)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-119)

## Organizational memberships

Ross is a past director of the Turnaround Management Association and member of its hall of fame.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-120) Ross has been the vice-chairman of the board of [Bank of Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Cyprus "Bank of Cyprus"), the largest bank in Cyprus, after he and his investors invested €400 million in the bank in 2014.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-121) As of January 2012, Ross was the leader (or "Grand Swipe") of the secret Wall Street fraternity, [Kappa Beta Phi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kappa_Beta_Phi "Kappa Beta Phi").[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-122) Ross served on the board of trustees of the [Brookings Institution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brookings_Institution "Brookings Institution"). He is also on the board of advisors of [Yale School of Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_School_of_Management "Yale School of Management") and is a former board member of the [Yale University Art Gallery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_University_Art_Gallery "Yale University Art Gallery").[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-yale-123) He served as International Counsel Member of the [Musée des Arts Décoratifs, Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musée_des_Arts_Décoratifs,_Paris "Musée des Arts Décoratifs, Paris"), and President of the American Friends of the [René Magritte Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/René_Magritte_Museum "René Magritte Museum") in Brussels.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-124) Ross has been on the [board of directors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_directors "Board of directors") of [Navigator Gas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navigator_Gas "Navigator Gas") since March 2012.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-tiestoputin-125)

## Political views

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Wilbur_Ross_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg/250px-Wilbur_Ross_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wilbur_Ross_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg)Ross speaking at a political conference in December 2018

### Support for Democratic Party and switch

Although he was an early supporter of [Donald Trump's presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump_2016_presidential_campaign "Donald Trump 2016 presidential campaign"), Ross was previously a registered [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"), served as an officer of the [New York State Democratic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Democratic_Committee "New York State Democratic Committee"), and held fundraisers for Democratic candidates at his apartment in New York City.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-bottomfeederking-2) He served under President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") on the board of [the U.S. Russia Investment Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_U.S._Russia_Investment_Fund "The U.S. Russia Investment Fund").

In January 1998, he funded $2.25 million in [seed money](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed_money "Seed money") into the campaign of his then-wife, [Betsy McCaughey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betsy_McCaughey "Betsy McCaughey"), who was seeking the Democratic nomination for [governor of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_York "Governor of New York").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-bottomfeederking-2) Since at least 2011, Ross has donated to Republican candidates and organizations.

Ross became a registered Republican in November 2016.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-126)

### Privatization

In the 1990s, New York City mayor [Rudy Giuliani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudy_Giuliani "Rudy Giuliani") appointed Ross as his [privatization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privatization "Privatization") advisor. He helped push to privatize the city's [public broadcasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_broadcasting "Public broadcasting") stations and the [Port Authority of New York and New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Authority_of_New_York_and_New_Jersey "Port Authority of New York and New Jersey"), and worked to sell off empty [land lots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_lot "Land lot") to businesses.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-127)

### Trade policy

Ross has described himself as "pro-sensible trade" and said that the U.S. government "should provide access to our markets to those countries who play fair, play by the rules and give everybody a fair chance to compete. Those who do not should not get away with it – they should be punished." Initially in favor of the [Trans-Pacific Partnership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trans-Pacific_Partnership "Trans-Pacific Partnership"), Ross has said that after examining the agreement, he found it was "not consistent with what was advertised".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-bottomfeederking-2)

In 2004, *[The Economist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Economist "The Economist")* described Ross as a supporter of [protectionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protectionism "Protectionism").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-128)

At the 2018 [World Economic Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Economic_Forum "World Economic Forum") in [Davos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davos "Davos"), Ross responded to concerns of a trade war by noting that "There have always been [trade wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_war "Trade war"). The difference now is U.S. troops are now coming to the [ramparts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rampart_(fortification) "Rampart (fortification)")."[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-129)

## Personal life

Ross married Judith Nodine in 1961. They divorced in 1995.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-fastfacts-6) After the divorce, Nodine sued Ross for failing to transfer stock by the agreed-upon deadline and Ross counter-sued.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-130) They had two children, Jessica Colby Ross (b. 1962) and Amanda Colby Ross (b. 1965). Amanda attended the [French Culinary Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Culinary_Institute "French Culinary Institute") and founded a baking company, while Jessica worked for [Sotheby's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sotheby's "Sotheby's").[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-131) In 1995, Ross married his second wife, [Lieutenant Governor of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_Governor_of_New_York "Lieutenant Governor of New York") [Betsy McCaughey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betsy_McCaughey "Betsy McCaughey"). They divorced in 2000.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-IsWilburCrazy-9)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-fastfacts-6) On October 9, 2004, Ross married his third wife, [Hilary Geary Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilary_Geary_Ross "Hilary Geary Ross"), a society writer for *[Quest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quest_(lifestyle_magazine) "Quest (lifestyle magazine)")* magazine.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-132)

In December 2016, while his Manhattan penthouse apartment at [The Briarcliffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Briarcliffe "The Briarcliffe") was on the market for $21 million,[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-observer-133) Ross purchased a 10,000 square foot house in the [Massachusetts Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Heights "Massachusetts Heights") neighborhood of [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), from [Adrienne Arsht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrienne_Arsht "Adrienne Arsht") for $10,750,000.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-134)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-135) In 2018, he purchased a $3.2 million house in [the Berkshires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Berkshires "The Berkshires"). He also owns two multimillion-dollar properties in [Palm Beach, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Beach,_Florida "Palm Beach, Florida").[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-136)

Ross owns an art collection valued at $150 million that includes pieces ranging from Western [surrealists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrealism "Surrealism") to contemporary Eastern sculptures. Ross owns 25 works by [René Magritte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/René_Magritte "René Magritte"), valued at $100 million, including some of the artist's most valuable paintings, such as *The Pilgrim*.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-137)

### Philanthropy

Ross donated $10 million for the construction of the new campus of [Yale School of Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_School_of_Management "Yale School of Management").[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross#cite_note-yale-123)
